report_question: What is the condition of this corpus and what should happen next?

findings.claim: Canonical authority is distributed across competing claims.
findings.interpretation: Several territories/files assert overlapping canonical/gold/final authority.
findings.consequence: Auto rename/move/dedupe could separate a source from its derivative or elevate an obsolete version.
findings.recommended_action: Run a non-mutating authority + dependency audit; produce a human ruling queue.
findings.automation_effect: Block path-changing automation until authority is resolved.

findings.claim: Canonical status cannot be inferred from filenames.
findings.interpretation: GOLD / CANONICAL / SOURCE_OF_TRUTH / FINAL are evidence of intent, not proof, and several coexist.
findings.consequence: Trusting a name would hard-code the wrong authority.
findings.recommended_action: Establish authority via references, modification history, and a user ruling.

findings.claim: A large share of the corpus may be generated or reproducible.
findings.interpretation: Markdown sources appear alongside html/xlsx/pdf exports of the same stems.
findings.consequence: Duplicate/archive decisions made before linking source→derivative would lose the source of truth.
findings.recommended_action: Link derivatives to sources before any dedupe or archive.
findings._warning: finding has no evidence — would be an invented narrative

findings.claim: Automatic reorganization currently has excessive blast radius.
findings.interpretation: Code, canonical material, generated outputs, and data coexist in scope.
findings.consequence: A single automated pass could break dependencies across unrelated systems.
findings.recommended_action: Operate report-only until dependencies and authority are mapped.

findings.interpretation: Identical content exists in multiple locations.
findings.consequence: Edits risk landing on the wrong copy; storage is wasted.
findings.recommended_action: Choose a governing location per group, then quarantine the rest.
